nguon.R1: Roché M., Li Z., Griffiths I. M., Le Roux S., Cantat I., Saint-Jalmes A., Stone H. A., 'Marangoni flow of soluble amphiphiles', Phys. Rev. Lett. 112, 208302 (2014); bản đọc arXiv 1312.3964v1 (_lam/nguon/roche.md). Đoạn mở: giọt nước pha nước rửa chén trên nước rắc tiêu, 'pepper grains are transported rapidly to the edge of the bowl' (movie M1); 'The flow results from the difference in surface tension'. Set-up (Fig. 1a, text): syringe pump Harvard PHD2000, lưu lượng mol không đổi Qa, kim, lớp nước dày cỡ cm ('centimeter-thick water layers'), nước Millipore 18.2 MΩ·cm, giọt dầu ô liu 10 μm làm tracer. Chất: 8 chất CnTABr (n 10–14), CnTACl (n 12, 16), CnNaSO4 (n 8–12), Sigma-Aldrich purity 99 %, cmc trải hai bậc. Fig. 1b: nguồn r_s, vùng trong suốt, ngoài có 'vortex pairs'; 'Further from the source, the tracers move only slightly'; dòng dưới 'follows the bottom of the container back towards the source'. Fig. 2a + text: r_t đổi 'over almost two orders of magnitude when n increases two-fold'; đổi C12TAB → C12NaSO4 (chỉ khác đầu) làm r_t giảm. Fig. 3a (Qa 0.52×10⁻⁶ mol/s): u ≈ 10⁻² m/s gần nguồn, 'maximum velocity u≈0.5 m/s', chậm dần 'as they travel across the transparent area', rồi 'decelerate abruptly'. Fig. 3b (C10NaSO4): 'The injection flow rate has little effect on the velocity field'. Mô hình: giả định dòng dừng khi chất 'have all desorbed from the interface'; Eq. 1 ℓν ≈ √(νr*/u*); Eq. 2 Sc ≈ 10⁴ (D 10⁻¹⁰, ν 10⁻⁶ m²/s); Eq. 3 c* = cmc; Eq. 5 cân bằng ứng suất; Eq. 6 u*; Eq. 7 r* ∝ (Qa/c*)^(3/4) (khớp Fig. 4c,d); A ≈ 1 (Fig. 4b), B gần 1; ước lượng c* 10⁻² M, A = B = 1 → u* ≈ 0.5 m/s, r* ≈ 15 mm 'compare very well with our experimental findings'; Eq. 6 hỏng khi vùng cỡ meniscus mm; lớp nhớt hơn → r_t lớn hơn (Fig. S5); đoạn kết: ước cmc 'from a single measurement of the size of the spreading area'. Bài KHÔNG nêu nhiệt độ.

beats.n: They tested eight surfactants, bought ninety nine per cent pure, with different tails and heads. Their micelle thresholds span two orders of magnitude. labels: friction in a thin moving layer
beats.n: Now the balance. The gap in pull, spread over the size of the soapy patch, must be matched by friction inside a thin moving layer of water. In Roché's model, viscosity times surface speed over that layer's thickness roughly equals the gap over the patch radius.

beats.src: Roché Eq. 5: η u*/ℓν ≈ (γw − γs)/r* (cân bằng ứng suất Marangoni với ứng suất nhớt trong lớp biên động lượng ℓν).

beats.n: Roché's model rests on one assumption: the flow stops when the injected surfactants have all desorbed from the interface. Past that point the surface is clean again, the pull is even, and nothing drives the flow. The ring marks where soap runs out on the surface.

beats.n: How fast should the surface go? Roché's speed law, with its constant set to one, uses the pull gap, viscosity, density and patch size. beats.n: So that is why the rush stops at a ring: in Roché's model, past it the soap has left the surface. And the ring is useful.
